drivingQuestion: Why is one who prays behind the synagogue called wicked, and what does the verse's closing phrase כרום זולות לבני אדם mean?
outcomeNote: Rav Huna's rule stands as qualified by Abaye. The exegesis of כרום זולות לבני אדם yields two competing readings (Rav Beivai's and R' Yoḥanan–R' Elazar's) that are left side by side, with the kerum bird supplied to support the second.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: כׇּל הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת נִקְרָא ״רָשָׁע״, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״סָבִיב רְשָׁעִים יִתְהַלָּכוּן״.
segments.en: Back to the topic of deference for a synagogue, the Gemara records that «Rav Huna said: One who prays behind the synagogue is called wicked,» as while the entire congregation is facing one direction to pray, he faces the opposite direction creating the impression that he is treating the synagogue and its congregation with contempt. «As it is stated: “The wicked walk round about,» when vileness is exalted among the sons of men” (Psalms 12:9). In other words, only the wicked walk round about the synagogue in order to pray.

segments.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא, אֲבָל מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא — לֵית לָן בַּהּ.
segments.en: «Abaye said: This» halakha «was said only» in a case «where one does not turn his face toward the synagogue. But» where «he turns his face toward the synagogue» and prays «we have no» prohibition «in» that case.

segments.he: הַהוּא גַבְרָא דְּקָא מְצַלֵּי אֲחוֹרֵי בֵּי כְּנִישְׁתָּא, וְלָא מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא. חֲלַף אֵלִיָּהוּ. חַזְיֵיהּ, אִידְּמִי לֵיהּ כְּטַיָּיעָא, אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּדוּ בָר קָיְימַתְּ קַמֵּי מָרָךְ?! שְׁלַף סַפְסֵרָא וְקַטְלֵיהּ.
segments.en: To reinforce the gravity of this prohibition, the Gemara relates: «A certain individual prayed behind the synagogue and did not turn to face the synagogue.» «Elijah» the Prophet «passed by and he saw him. He appeared to» him «as an Arab [taya’a].» Elijah «said: “This is how [kadu bar] you stand before your Master?”» Elijah «drew a sword and killed him.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי לְרַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי ״כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם״?
segments.en: Rav Huna already explained the beginning of the verse, “The wicked walk round about.” The Gemara explains the end of the verse: “When vileness is exalted among the sons of men.” «One of the Sages said to Rav Beivai bar Abaye, and some say Rav Beivai» said to «Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak: What is» the meaning of: «“When vileness is exalted among the sons of men”?»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵלּוּ דְּבָרִים שֶׁעוֹמְדִים בְּרוּמוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, וּבְנֵי אָדָם מְזַלְזְלִין בָּהֶן.
segments.en: «He said to him: These are matters of utmost importance,» exalted, i.e., mitzvot or prayer, «which people» nonetheless «treat with contempt,» vileness among the sons of men.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּצְטָרֵךְ אָדָם לַבְּרִיּוֹת, פָּנָיו מִשְׁתַּנּוֹת כִּכְרוּם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כְּרֻם זֻלּוּת לִבְנֵי אָדָם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan and» his student, «Rabbi Elazar, both said» an alternative explanation of this verse: «Once a person needs» the help of «others» and loses dignity in their eyes, vileness among the sons of men, «his face changes» and becomes «like a kerum, as it is stated: “When [kerum] vileness is exalted among the sons of men.”»

segments.he: מַאי ״כְּרוּם״? כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אָמַר: עוֹף אֶחָד יֵשׁ בִּכְרַכֵּי הַיָּם, וּ״כְרוּם״ שְׁמוֹ, וְכֵיוָן שֶׁחַמָּה זוֹרַחַת מִתְהַפֵּךְ לְכַמָּה גְּווֹנִין.
segments.en: «What is kerum» referred to by Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rabbi Elazar? «When Rav Dimi came» to Babylonia from Eretz Yisrael «he said: There is a bird in the cities by the sea called kerum and when the sun rises,» the bird «changes several colors.» Similarly, one who becomes dependent upon others blushes in embarrassment.

segments.he: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ: כְּאִלּוּ נִדּוֹן בִּשְׁנֵי דִינִים, אֵשׁ וּמַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִרְכַּבְתָּ אֱנוֹשׁ לְרֹאשֵׁנוּ בָּאנוּ בָאֵשׁ וּבַמַּיִם״.
segments.en: «Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi both said:» One who becomes dependent upon others, «it is as if he was punished with two punishments: Fire and water. As it is stated: “You have caused men to ride over our heads; we have gone through fire and water”» (Psalms 66:12).
